openQuestions.for: the lane lead and the boards
openQuestions.question: In Dawn the one state colour (--gold, #9a7f5e) measures about 3.4:1 on the card, so the proposal eyebrow and the recorded line's gold word sit between the two tiers.
openQuestions.howItIsHeldNow: The state colour is held to the 3.0:1 tier only where it is marking a state: the element carries a marker or eyebrow class, or its text is shorter than 24 characters (review R1 SHOULD FIX 11). Gold on a paragraph is body copy and keeps 4.5:1. Nothing in app/ was changed.
openQuestions.whatWouldChange: If the boards want the gold to carry 4.5:1 in Dawn even as a marker, the Dawn --gold token changes and GOLD_MARKER_CLASSES in quality/common.py goes. Eleven Dawn states would FAIL until then.

openQuestions.question: The disabled Save button's label measures 3.3:1 in Dawn (app.css:222 dims a disabled control to 55% opacity), on T-07, T-44 and T-48.
openQuestions.howItIsHeldNow: A disabled control's label is held to the 3.0:1 tier, because STANDARD.md section 10 already calls a disabled primary's label a muted label.
openQuestions.whatWouldChange: Nothing, unless the standard decides an inactive control must still carry 4.5:1.

openQuestions.question: The state record thumbnail is 1/16 scale, not the 1/8 the ticket named.
openQuestions.howItIsHeldNow: At 1/8 a 3 px shift, which the rect half of the tolerance allows, already moves the thumbnail 3.5 levels and would fail the thumbnail half, so the tolerance would contradict itself and mutation h1 could not pass. At 1/16 the same shift moves it 1.7 and a 60 px shift moves it 8.5. The tree is 1256 files and 1.4 MB with both platforms' thumbnails in it, inside the 3 MB budget.
openQuestions.whatWouldChange: Nothing, unless the rect tolerance tightens below 3 px, in which case the scale can go back.

openQuestions.question: The win32 screen baselines do not exist yet.
openQuestions.howItIsHeldNow: The mechanism is keyed on sys.platform and a missing baseline for the current platform is a FAIL naming the exact path and the remedy, so a Windows run today reports six FAILs and no vacuous pass.
openQuestions.whatWouldChange: The lane lead runs "python quality/gate.py --accept" on the owner PC before the branch is offered, and commits quality/baseline/win32/, ENV.txt included. The win32 state thumbnails already exist, under quality/baseline/states/win32/; their ENV.txt arrives with the lead's next "python quality/statesheet.py --accept" run.

openQuestions.question: quality/common.py is a file the ticket did not name.
openQuestions.howItIsHeldNow: It holds only what gate.py and statesheet.py must agree on: the copy sweeps, the contrast tiers with the muted class list, the label font chain and the refusal type. The word sweep bug existed in one gate and not the other, which is the drift this file exists to stop. No new dependency.
openQuestions.whatWouldChange: If the lane wants one file per gate, the constants are duplicated and a test has to hold them equal.

openQuestions.question: "fits without scrolling at 393x852" was a WARN and is now a FAIL, because WARN is reserved for the type scale and the spacing scale.
openQuestions.howItIsHeldNow: It passes on all six prototype renders today. The chassis is designed to scroll, so a later ticket that grows the default Today could turn this into a FAIL for a screen that is behaving as ruled.
openQuestions.whatWouldChange: Either the check is retired, or it stays and a scrolling default is a decision the ticket records. Nothing in this ticket depends on it.

openQuestions.question: teeth.py runs the gate rows with --screens and --sizes narrowed to the screen the change is on, to stay inside the 25 minute budget (19 rows in 462 s).
openQuestions.howItIsHeldNow: The narrowed run is the same code on fewer iterations, and --accept refuses to run with either flag so a partial baseline cannot be written. Review R1 is right that it is not the same evidence: the full gate also raises the regression rows on the screens the narrowed run drops, so a row asserts the named refusal only. The teeth.py docstring says so now.
openQuestions.whatWouldChange: A hand re-run of any row with the full gate takes about two minutes per row and should report the same FAIL plus the regression rows the change also moves.

openQuestions.question: A baseline carries no provenance. A hand written quality/baseline/win32/ full of another platform's renders would sit there unread on a Linux run (review R1, NOTES).
openQuestions.howItIsHeldNow: An accept run labels its own report, no report is committed, and README section 3.1 now says in one line that a reviewer reads the baseline diff in the pull request.
openQuestions.whatWouldChange: A stronger guard would sign the baseline directory with the ENV.txt it was drawn under and refuse a set whose ENV.txt does not match the running machine, which would also refuse every legitimate machine upgrade. Not taken.

openQuestions.question: The record's visible text is now the text of the elements that survive the visibility test, joined in document order, rather than innerText (review R1 SHOULD FIX 1).
openQuestions.howItIsHeldNow: It is the only way a line hidden at opacity 0 can read as removed, which is what the review asked for. visibility: hidden leaves the record by the same test, where before it left only because innerText excluded it.
openQuestions.whatWouldChange: Every record was rewritten with --accept for it. A reviewer comparing an old record to a new one will see the text field change shape on states with hidden content.

openQuestions.question: what the per platform thumbnail split is NOT protected by. A committed thumbnail that is byte identical to another platform's file of the same name is now a FAIL (review R3 SHOULD FIX 2), and that catches a copy.
